subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: Toyota Unintended Acceleration
description: A fast breakdown of Toyota Unintended Acceleration for builders.

hook.text: Toyotas suddenly accelerated without driver input. 89 people died. Investigators found software spaghetti code.

buildup.text: From 2002 to 2009, Toyota received thousands of complaints about unintended acceleration in multiple models.

discovery.text: NASA investigators found the throttle software had 10,000+ global variables and no failsafe task monitoring.

twist.text: Toyota blamed floor mats and driver error for years. The software wasn't independently tested until lawsuits forced it.

climax.text: Toyota paid $1.2 billion in fines. The case became a landmark for automotive software safety regulation.

punchline.text: 10,000 global variables. No watchdog. Cars that drove themselves.

quiz.question: What did NASA find in Toyota's throttle software?
options: 10,000+ global variables and no failsafe monitoring
